page: The Vultr vhp-8c-16gb-intel is an entry-tier compute-oriented instance within the High Performance family, provisioned with 8 shared vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores of an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.0 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture, the processor features 16 MB of L3 cache, 4 MB of L2 cache, and vector instruction support including AVX, AVX-512F, and AVX-512_VNNI, alongside hardware acceleration for AES cryptography.

Memory capacity is configured at 16.0 GB, establishing a 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The server bundles a single 350 GB NVMe SSD for fast local persistence and includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. The configuration contains no dedicated GPU accelerators.

Benchmark outcomes show mid-tier throughput across general multithreaded and I/O tasks, counterbalanced by modest single-threaded performance. The server achieved a Geekbench multi-core score of 5786.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 12523.23, while Geekbench single-core performance registered at 1090.0, placing it in the lower quartile. Memory bandwidth remains solid with 62.89 GB/sec read and 44.5 GB/sec write on uncached blocks. Application tests demonstrate balanced results, delivering 12.74 million Redis SET operations per second and 8.38 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. CPU-based machine learning inference on larger models is constrained, generating only 5.01 tokens per second on a 7B parameter LLM.

Given its shared CPU core model and moderate memory allotment, the vhp-8c-16gb-intel provides cost efficiency for multi-threaded batch jobs, software compilation (scoring 10363.0 in Clang build benchmarks), web serving, and mid-sized database workloads that benefit from NVMe storage rather than peak single-thread execution.
description: The Vultr vhp-8c-16gb-intel is a High Performance series virtual machine featuring 8 shared vCPUs across 4 physical cores on an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor clocked at 2.0 GHz. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of RAM, a 16 MB L3 cache, and instruction support including AVX-512 and AES. Bundled with 350 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and one IPv4 address, the configuration lacks dedicated GPU acceleration. Benchmark evaluations show balanced multi-core execution, yielding a PassMark CPU score of 12523.23, a Geekbench multi-core score of 5786.0, and static web serving throughput of 8.38 GB/sec. However, single-core processing is modest with a Geekbench score of 1090.0. This compute-to-RAM balance makes the instance suitable for distributed web services, compilation pipelines, caching layers, and database workloads relying on local NVMe throughput.
